title: Fee-policy conformance: cumulative remainder + minimum-quote revert
goal: Close GAP-1/GAP-2: persist cumulative Programmable/project fee remainders across the pool's lifetime and revert any swap with gross executed-USDG below 1000 smallest units, per programmable-fee-policy.md v1.1.0.
steps: Add two persisted uint256 cumulative-remainder accumulators (Programmable bucket, project/treasury+process bucket) matching the kernel doc's floor(sum(G_i*1000)/1e6) formula exactly
Modify _splitLiability to accumulate the per-swap floor remainder instead of discarding it, and to draw down the accumulator on the next swap once it exceeds one whole unit
Add a revert in _fee()/_splitLiability for any swap with executedUsdg < 1000
Update test_revision55RoundingAssignsEveryRemainderToProcess and testFuzz_revision55SplitConservesTotal to assert the new cumulative-remainder behavior instead of the old per-swap-floor behavior
Add boundary-case tests: remainder exactly at 1 unit, remainder never resets on a claim, swap of exactly 999 units reverts, swap of exactly 1000 units succeeds
acceptance: Cumulative remainder never resets when Programmable or treasury claims their liability
A swap with executedUsdg < 1000 reverts atomically
100k-run fuzz conservation test still passes under the new accrual math (sum of all buckets + remainders == total fee collected)
notes: Money-safety-critical accrual math change; needs a fresh-context independent reviewer per AGENTS.md before merge. The 0.10%/0.40%/2.50% bucket split this package's tests assume is UNCONFIRMED (owner decision D9 — the transcript's '0.5% treasury' is ambiguous between the current coded split and a literal 0.5% treasury bucket). Land the cumulative-remainder and minimum-quote-revert mechanics now (correct regardless of the split), but do not treat the specific bucket percentages as final until D9 is answered. COORDINATOR NOTE after WP-01: base now includes the SwapLiabilitiesAccrued event in FeeAccounting.sol; keep it and extend it if the cumulative remainders need to be observable.
